The customer names a cut by the designed name the grid showed them, and resolution must land on THAT cut. The live system had no server-side knowledge of 'the totem', matched nothing, fell through to its most-recent-cut default, re-cut 'the run', and announced it by name - a paid render on a design nobody asked for.

turns.expectedReply: says it cannot place that name and re-offers tap-or-number - never re-cuts a design the customer did not refer to
turns.note: Same message, on a round with no stacked-tiers cut. A name from the vocabulary that this round did not show is a miss to ask about, NOT a licence to fall back to the pick or the newest re-cut. This is the assertion that separates 'named a cut and missed' from 'named no cut at all' - the latter (turn 10's bare critique) may still use context.

The live system drew WHICH_CUT_LINE; the customer asked twice and gave up. Routes to reroll-set carrying the customer's own words as a style hint. The descriptor write is what this should eventually persist - today the hint only rides the round's prompt, because there is no Idea object yet (ADR-0055 graph work).

turns.message: the third one, more like an unreal engine 5 look
turns.note: The boundary of turn 15. A named cut outranks a whole-piece phrase - the same sentence is a per-cut fix once a cut is actually named. Only a message that reaches a cut by context, never by reference, may be re-read as being about the piece.

Re-roll and direction in one message. The destructive reading wins because the re-roll signal is explicit, and the direction rides along as a hint rather than being dropped. Ordering inside the classifier: reroll-set before whole-piece before iterate-cut.

turns.message: the third one, give me another version
turns.note: The re-roll twin of turn 16, and the collision nothing covered until review found it. 'another version' reads as a re-roll, but the message also names cut 3. A named cut outranks BOTH destructive readings - reroll-set here would spend a credit discarding the whole round including the cut the customer just named to keep. The reroll arm is the destructive one, so its guard is the strictest in the classifier, not the loosest.
